alt: A complaint (PHAR-20260316-54013) was filed by Nicolas Hernandez against CVS Pharmacy #09785 (PHY 46377) located at 2006 W Avenue J, Lancaster, CA, regarding Pharmacist Hoang Dang (RPH #52538) who on March 15, 2026, allegedly refused to dispense Buprenorphine/naloxone, claiming it was "out of stock," but the medication was later partially filled on March 16, 2026, by Pharmacist Katie Nguyen at the same location.

• Hoang Dang - Pharmacist - RPH #52538

Please briefly describe your complaint
• I am filing a formal complaint for Unprofessional Conduct (BPC § 4301) and Obstruction of Therapy (BPC § 733). On March 15, 2026, Pharmacist Hoang Dang (RPH 52538) informed me my prescription was "out of stock" after a performative, zero-second inventory check. Less than an hour later, Pharmacist Katie Nguyen successfully filled the same prescription at the same location. The medication was provided as a partial-fill in a plastic baggie, proving the bulk stock was physically present during Dang's initial refusal. RPH Dang intentionally falsified inventory status to deny service and obstruct my medical treatment. I request a review of the Electronic Pedigree and Inventory Reconciliation Reports for both March 15 and March 16, 2026. I suspect the "Out of Stock" status was a result of manual inventory manipulation intended to obstruct dispensing, as the medication was immediately available for a partial fill by a different pharmacist (Nguyen) on 3/16 without a delivery taking place.

If your prescription pick-up/delivery was delayed and you were without medication, approximately how many days did you or the person the prescription was for go without medication?
• On Sunday, March 15, I called CVS #09785 at 3:23 PM and spoke with RPh Hoang Dang (52538) for over 7 minutes. He intentionally obstructed my care by falsely claiming the medication was out of stock. Later that evening at 9:45 PM, I spoke with RPh Katie Nguyen, who contradicted his claim and facilitated a partial fill from the bulk stock Dang claimed did not exist. This 6+ hour intentional delay disrupted my strict, medically supervised benzodiazepine taper. By refusing to dispense my maintenance medication in bad faith, RPh Dang triggered acute withdrawal symptoms, physical instability, and severe psychological distress. His fabricated "out of stock" claim was a direct threat to my safety and a violation of the standard of care.

• Intentional deception by a pharmacist creates immediate medical risk. For maintenance medications like Buprenorphine, a refusal to dispense can lead to withdrawal, medical instability, and severe emotional distress. RPh Dang's bad-faith obstruction forced me to involve a second pharmacist (Nguyen) to receive the care I am legally entitled to under BPC § 733.
